Prepare data for ccflowR visualization

Source: R/export.R
prepare_for_ccflowr.Rd

Prepare ContextResult data in a format ready for direct use with the ccflowR R package for signaling flow visualization. ccflowR is an R package that can be used directly in R without needing to export files to disk.

prepare_for_ccflowr(
  result,
  expression_data = NULL,
  sender = NULL,
  receiver = NULL,
  top_n_ligands = 20,
  framework = c("nichenet", "multinichenet")
)

Arguments

result

A ContextResult object from predict_ligand_activity_nichenet()

expression_data

Optional expression matrix or Seurat object for extracting ligand/receptor expression levels

sender

Sender cell type(s) to include

receiver

Receiver cell type(s) to include

top_n_ligands

Maximum number of ligands to include (default: 20)

framework

Output format: "nichenet" or "multinichenet" (default: "nichenet")

Value

A data.frame ready for ccflowR visualization functions (e.g., ccflowR::sankey_plot()) with columns: sender, ligand, receptor, receiver, scaled_activity, scaled_ligand_expression, scaled_receptor_expression

Details

This is the recommended way to visualize ContextNet results with ccflowR. The ccflowR package is an R package that provides sankey/river plots, heatmaps, and other signaling flow visualizations directly in R.

The output data.frame is designed for ccflowR's flow-conserving edge weight computation:

  • scaled_activity: Ligand activity score (AUPR-based)

  • scaled_ligand_expression: Scaled expression of ligand in sender

  • scaled_receptor_expression: Scaled expression of receptor in receiver

For MultiNicheNet-style output (differential analysis), additional columns are included: prioritization_score, scaled_lfc_ligand, scaled_lfc_receptor.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# After running analysis
result <- predict_ligand_activity_nichenet(seurat_obj, network, ...)

# Prepare for ccflowR (direct R package integration)
sankey_data <- prepare_for_ccflowr(result, seurat_obj,
                                    sender = "Macrophage",
                                    receiver = "Fibroblast")

# Use directly with ccflowR in R (no file export needed)
if (requireNamespace("ccflowR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ccflowR::sankey_plot(sankey_data, colors = cell_colors)
}
} # }
